    ZarrSparseMatrix

    A DelayedArray backend for sparse matrices stored in Zarr.

    ZarrSparseMatrix reads a sparse matrix saved in a Zarr group as the three 1D arrays data, indices and indptr, in CSR or CSC layout. This is how AnnData’s write_zarr() stores its X matrix. The matrix stays on disk and is read with Rarr only when needed. It is the Zarr counterpart of HDF5Array::H5SparseMatrix.

    Because a ZarrSparseMatrix is a DelayedMatrix, it works with any code written for DelayedArray objects: subsetting, rowSums()/colSums(), block processing, delayed arithmetic, and assays in a SingleCellExperiment.

    Installation 

    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("Rarr", "DelayedArray", "SparseArray"))

# Install from Bioconductor
BiocManager::install("ZarrSparseMatrix")

# Install from GitHub
# remotes::install_github("GabrielHoffman/ZarrSparseMatrix")

    Usage 

    library(ZarrSparseMatrix)

# Example store: 200 cells x 100 genes, in AnnData's CSR layout
store <- system.file("extdata", "example.zarr", package = "ZarrSparseMatrix")
X <- ZarrSparseMatrix(store, "X")
X
#> <200 x 100> sparse ZarrSparseMatrix object of type "integer":

X[1:5, 1:10]          # delayed subsetting
colSums(X)            # computed block by block
as(X, "dgCMatrix")    # load into memory

# Genes as rows: transposing the seed turns CSR into CSC without reading data
counts <- ZarrSparseMatrix(t(seed(X)))

library(SingleCellExperiment)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts))

    The dimensions and layout are read from the group’s shape and encoding-type attributes. If they are missing, pass dim and sparse.layout. Row and column names can be given with dimnames.

    See the vignette for more examples:

    vignette("ZarrSparseMatrix")

    Writing a store from Python

    Use Zarr format 2. Rarr reads Zarr v2 arrays, and recent anndata versions are switching their default to v3:

    import anndata as ad

ad.settings.zarr_write_format = 2
adata.write_zarr("data.zarr")
    X <- ZarrSparseMatrix("data.zarr", "X")

    Limitations

    • Only Zarr v2 stores have been tested.
    • Only local stores have been tested.
    • Rarr::write_zarr_array() writes the last chunk of an array shorter than the other chunks. Rarr’s own reader then fails on indexed reads that touch that chunk. Stores written by zarr-python and anndata are not affected. inst/scripts/make-example-data.R shows how to write a compatible store from R.
